text:
Alex: FYI we've seen intermittent packet drops between GPU nodes in us-west-2 this morning, overlay only (vxlan). Some training jobs observed 5-10% p99 RPC retries.
Maria: saw the alert too — which podset?
Alex: mostly on the reserved-gpu pools, pods on nodes gpux-*-w2. Correlates with high egress from GPU batches.
Sam: timeline? is it persistent or bursts?
Alex: bursts that last ~30-90s, then clear. Happened ~08:12, 08:43, 09:05. Noticed increased retransmits in our app logs.
Devon: can you dump `ip -s link` and `ethtool -S`? suspect offload/segmentation issues with encapsulation.
Alex: copying snippet from one affected node:
```
$ ip -s link show vxlan0
4: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1400 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 12345678 packets 98765 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0 frame 0
    TX: bytes 23456789 packets 123456 errors 0 dropped 12 overruns 0 carrier 0 collisions 0
```
`ethtool -k eth0` shows GSO/TSO/GRO on.
Maria: MTU 1400 on vxlan0 — that matches our overlay headroom. But drops in TX counter on vxlan, could be segmentation offload interacting with encapsulation.
Kevin: any firmware or driver updates recently on Mellanox NICs? we pushed a firmware roll last week to some pools.
Sam: good call. I saw a firmware push to gpux-*-w2 on 2026-03-10. Might coincide.
Alex: we captured tcpdump during a burst: large encapsulated packets arriving but peers not acking. Saving pcap now.
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-20260310-17, paging eng-sre.
Devon: quick repro commands we used earlier:
```
# generate sustained single-connection traffic across nodes
iperf3 -c <peer> -P 1 -t 120 -f m
# capture on host (overlay interface)
sudo tcpdump -i vxlan0 -s 0 -w /tmp/vxlan-burst.pcap
# check offload stats
ethtool -k eth0
```
Maria: also check `dmesg` for NIC offload drops and `sysctl net.core.netdev_max_backlog`. If queue overflows under bursts, kernel might drop before encapsulation.
Kevin: I pulled NIC counters from affected node — no hardware rx errors, but driver shows header split failures on some Mellanox cards (MLX5).
Sam: header split failures = firmware/driver interaction with GSO + encapsulation often. On older kernels we've seen it when inner packet > MTU and NIC tries header-splitting.
Alex: actioned: disabled GSO/TSO on eth0 on one node and started a heavy job. Early result: no overlay tx drops during the burst window.
Maria: good signal. Can you run with GSO off for a few nodes and monitor latency and CPU? GSO off increases CPU load, might affect throughput.
Alex: will do. Also tried bumping vxlan MTU to 1450 temporarily (inner MTU still 1500 on pod iface), observed fewer retransmits but need broader test.
Devon: long-term options: (1) firmware patch from Mellanox that fixes header-split with encapsulation, (2) ensure host MTU/encap configs give enough headroom, (3) enable offload-aware encapsulation in kernel (if available), or (4) keep GSO off with faster CPUs for these pools.
Kevin: I'll open a support ticket with Mellanox and include pcaps + ethtool outputs.
oncall-bot: added runbook steps to incident INC-20260310-17 (probe->mitigation->rollback).
Sam: also check kube-proxy/ipvs conntrack handling — I saw conntrack entries spike during bursts, might aggravate recovery.
Maria: noted. For mitigation now: 1) cordon + drain a couple nodes and flip offload flags, 2) restrict large-batch jobs to a test pool, 3) notify ML infra owners.
Alex: doing step 1 on gpux-23-w2, gpux-29-w2 now. Draining + disabling GSO on hosts.
Kevin: putting an alert to detect <95% tx success on vxlan devices so we catch next burst earlier.
Sam: keep an eye on CPU on hosts with GSO off. If CPU becomes the bottleneck we'll need fallback (smaller batch sizes, or move jobs to dedicated hosts).
Maria: thanks team — keep updates here. If Mellanox responds with firmware fix we'll coordinate a controlled rollout. :thumbsup:
Alex: pcap uploaded to incident with notes. I'll post perf numbers after 2 hours.
Kevin: created support case MLX-7892 with the vendor.
Maria: relocating some non-urgent training runs out of us-west-2 as a short-term capacity relief.
Alex: update 09:50 — after disabling offloads on 3 nodes we've seen no packet drops in subsequent bursts, CPU up ~12%, app latency stable.
Devon: good. Plan: vendor firmware + kernel/config delta to re-enable offload safely.
Sam: add an e2e test for encapsulation under GSO enabled so we don't regress.
Maria: agreed. Closing current incident if next 24h looks clean.
Alex: thanks everyone.
